title: Secrets Management
summary: Secrets management keeps passwords, API keys, and certificates out of code and config files. A workload proves who it is using the platform's built-in identity, so no 'secret zero' has to be distributed. A policy check decides what it may read, and secrets are stored encrypted under keys that never leave a KMS or HSM. Better still, dynamic secrets are created on demand and expire within hours, so a leak is short-lived.

walkthrough.title: Authenticate with platform identity
walkthrough.text: A pod presents its Kubernetes service-account JWT (or a cloud IAM role). The vault verifies it with the platform and maps it to a role, so no password ever has to be planted on the machine.

walkthrough.title: Check policy, write the audit log
walkthrough.text: The role's policy allows read on secret/data/payments/* only. Every request, allowed or denied, is written to a tamper-evident audit log before any answer is returned.

walkthrough.title: Decrypt with envelope encryption
walkthrough.text: The stored secret is ciphertext under a data key, and the data key is itself encrypted by a root key held in a KMS or HSM. The vault asks the KMS to unwrap the data key and then decrypts the secret in memory.

walkthrough.title: Return a short-lived result
walkthrough.text: The workload receives the secret with a lease and its own short-lived token, ideally injected into a file or memory rather than environment variables that end up in logs.

walkthrough.title: Create dynamic credentials
walkthrough.text: For the database, the vault instead creates a unique user right now, CREATE ROLE v-payments-x7 VALID UNTIL +1h, so every pod has its own credentials that can be traced.

walkthrough.title: Renew while in use
walkthrough.text: The workload's agent renews the lease while the pod runs, and the app reloads credentials on rotation without restarting.

walkthrough.title: Expire and revoke
walkthrough.text: When the lease ends or the pod dies, the vault drops the database user. A leaked credential is useless within the hour, and one command can revoke everything a compromised role was given.

data.label: Workload

input.name: Secrets
input.type: Mounted file or in-memory value + lease

responsibilities: Proves its identity using what the platform already provides.
Fetches secrets at runtime, never baking them into images or Git.
Renews leases and reloads rotated credentials.

failureModes.scenario: Secret printed in logs or crash dumps
failureModes.impact: Credentials spread to log systems and tickets.
failureModes.mitigation: Avoid env vars for secrets; redaction in log pipelines; short TTLs.

failureModes.impact: Pods cannot start during an incident.
failureModes.mitigation: Agent caching, retries with backoff, highly available vault clusters.

data.label: Secrets Service
responsibilities: Verifies workload identity with the platform and issues short-lived tokens.
Enforces policy on every path and operation.
Manages leases, renewal, and revocation.

failureModes.impact: New pods and rotations fail across the company.
failureModes.mitigation: Multi-node HA, regional replicas, and cached leases in agents.
Revoke root tokens after setup; break-glass procedure with multiple key holders.

data.label: Policies & Audit
responsibilities: Grants each role only the paths it needs (least privilege).
Records every access for forensics and compliance.
Refuses requests if the audit log cannot be written.

failureModes.mitigation: Per-service paths; policy review; alerts on broad grants.

failureModes.impact: Vault blocks all requests (it fails closed).
failureModes.mitigation: Multiple audit devices and monitoring of their health.

data.label: Encrypted Storage

output.name: Read
output.type: Ciphertext only: useless without the KMS

responsibilities: Persists only encrypted data; a disk or backup leak reveals nothing.
Keeps versions of each secret for rollback.
Replicates across nodes for availability.

failureModes.impact: Secrets lost permanently in a disaster.
failureModes.mitigation: Scheduled restore drills including KMS access.

failureModes.impact: Leaked old versions still valid elsewhere.
failureModes.mitigation: Rotate at the source and prune old versions.

data.label: KMS / HSM
responsibilities: Holds the root key in tamper-resistant hardware that never exports it.
Unwraps data keys for authorised callers only.
Supports key rotation without re-encrypting all data immediately.

failureModes.scenario: KMS key deleted or access lost
failureModes.mitigation: Deletion waiting periods, tight IAM on key admin, multi-region keys.
Cache unwrapped data keys in memory for a bounded time.

data.label: Dynamic Secrets Engine
responsibilities: Creates unique, short-lived credentials on demand.
Revokes them automatically when leases expire.
Issues short-lived certificates from an internal CA as well.

failureModes.impact: Expired users linger in the database.
failureModes.mitigation: Retry revocation; a periodic sweep for orphaned users.

failureModes.scenario: Thousands of pods each creating DB users
failureModes.impact: Database user table and auth load explode.
failureModes.mitigation: Longer TTLs for stable pools, or a connection proxy with its own identity.

data.label: Target Database

input.name: Admin SQL
input.type: CREATE ROLE … VALID UNTIL …; DROP ROLE …

output.name: Access
output.type: Workload connects with its own short-lived user

responsibilities: Accepts users created by the vault with scoped grants.
Attributes every query to a specific workload instance.
Rotates the vault's own admin password regularly.

failureModes.scenario: Vault's admin credential is too powerful
failureModes.impact: Vault compromise means full database compromise.
failureModes.mitigation: Admin role that can only create and drop scoped roles.

failureModes.impact: Errors when the user is dropped mid-use.
failureModes.mitigation: Pools refresh credentials before lease expiry.
